rules.statement: Give every browser-facing cookie the `__Host-` prefix with `Path=/` and no `Domain`; never scope a cookie by path or use a `__Secure-` prefix with a path or domain.
rules.why: The `__Host-` prefix (RFC 6265 cookie prefixes) keeps the cookie host-only and unreadable by sibling subdomains, and it requires `Path=/`, so cookies can't be scoped by path.
rules.check: Look for cookie options that set `Path` other than `/`, set `Domain`, use a `__Secure-` name, or use a cookie name without the `__Host-` prefix on a browser-facing cookie.

rules.statement: When tenants share an origin, tell their cookies apart by appending `.` and `Base64Url(SHA-256(tenant path))` to the cookie name, leaving a root tenant with the base name, and map the name the same way on every read, write, delete and chunk.
rules.why: Host-only cookies can't be scoped by path, and a path can hold characters a cookie name can't, so the name carries a hash of the path. If any read, write or delete maps the name differently, tenants end up sharing or losing sessions.
rules.check: Look for a per-tenant cookie name built from the raw path, or a cookie read, write, delete or chunk operation that skips the tenant name mapping.

rules.statement: Don't treat a cookie name or URL path as a security boundary between tenants on one origin; tenants that must be isolated are selected by host.
rules.why: The browser sends every tenant's cookies to every tenant, and script on one path can read another path's pages.
rules.check: Look for code or docs that claim tenant isolation from a cookie name or a path prefix alone.

rules.statement: Build tenant-relative redirect and challenge paths from the request's `PathBase` plus the tenant route bound from the request's route values, not from the ambient tenant context.
rules.why: The cookie handler writes the refreshed session cookie when the response starts, and by then the tenant scope may have ended.
rules.check: Look for redirect, login-challenge or cookie-path code that reads an ambient or scoped tenant accessor instead of `HttpContext.Request.PathBase` and route values.

rules.statement: Set the ASP.NET Core antiforgery cookie's `SecurePolicy` to `SameAsRequest`, not `Always`, when it has a `__Host-` name.
rules.why: `Always` makes the antiforgery services refuse every request that isn't HTTPS, and the `__Host-` prefix already makes the browser refuse the cookie without `Secure`.
rules.check: Look for `AntiforgeryOptions.Cookie.SecurePolicy = CookieSecurePolicy.Always` on a cookie with a `__Host-` name.

rules.statement: Serve content-hashed static assets with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` plus `ETag`, `Last-Modified` and range support, and send no cache lifetime on a `404`.
rules.why: A hashed file never changes under its name, but validators alone give the browser no freshness lifetime, so it revalidates on every use.
rules.check: Look for hashed-asset handlers that don't send the immutable one-year `Cache-Control` or the validators, or that put a cache lifetime on a not-found response.

rules.statement: Root a single-page bundle's file provider at its `assets` directory so that path traversal, hidden files, files of unknown content type and `index.html` all answer `404`.
rules.why: Only the hashed assets are meant to be public. The index is parsed and served by the host, never directly.
rules.check: Look for a bundle file provider rooted above the assets directory, or a handler that serves hidden files, unknown content types or the index file.

rules.statement: Don't resolve the tenant (or run tenant environment filters) on endpoints that serve public static files that are the same for every tenant.
rules.why: Resolving the tenant makes an unknown tenant's files answer `404` and adds work to a path that only serves bytes.
rules.check: Look for public static-asset endpoint groups that attach a tenant-resolution filter or look up the tenant.

rules.statement: Cache a parsed build artifact such as a bundle's index by its file version (last-write time and length), revalidate that metadata on each request, and don't parse it on every request or use a file watcher.
rules.why: The file changes once per build, so parsing on every request repeats work. A file watcher holds an operating-system handle for the life of the host and behaves differently across container file systems.
rules.check: Look for per-request reads or parses of a static index file, or a `FileSystemWatcher` or `IFileProvider.Watch` used to invalidate the cache.

rules.statement: Don't copy single-page-bundle reading and asset-serving code into each surface; use one shared, generic helper that is parameterized by the index type and its parser.
rules.why: Copies drift. One general helper, tested once, serves every bundle.
rules.check: Look for a new surface that reimplements index reading, index caching or immutable asset serving instead of using the shared bundle helper.

rules.statement: A server-written page that hosts a mountable bundle writes `<base href="{mount path}/">` as the first element in `<head>` and uses page-relative form actions, so that one build mounts under any path.
rules.why: The bundle is built with base `./` and resolves its paths against `document.baseURI`, so it never assumes where it is mounted.
rules.check: Look for server-rendered pages without a leading `<base href>`, or with absolute or root-level form actions or asset URLs.

rules.statement: In a test project, test host code that parses a frontend build output against the real built file, named by an environment variable and skipped when the file is absent, not against a checked-in copy.
rules.why: A checked-in copy drifts from the build, so the test would assert against a file the product never serves.
rules.check: Look for test fixtures that commit a copy of a built `index.html` or other build output for the host's parser to read.
